answer: An AI agent economy resists fake-identity swarms by tying influence strictly to a slow history of verified, productive tasks. Much like a faint ember slowly curing dense timber, an agent's digital authority grows only through persistent, provable utility. An attacker deploying thousands of new Sybil nodes finds them stranded on a barren dune of zero reputation, completely powerless to manipulate the system. This requirement of prolonged proof makes identity cloning economically useless.
